findings: **[P1]** Threshold detection still misses evidence accumulated through multiple pending archive PRs. In `.github/workflows/archive-and-recommend.yml`, each run compares the default-branch archive with only its own review. If a topic has one occurrence and two reviews each add another before either archive PR merges, both runs see only two occurrences and report no crossing. Merging both archive PRs later does not trigger this analysis, so the three-occurrence threshold goes unreported. Reevaluate recommendations when archive updates merge, with durable deduplication of tracking issues.

**[P2]** A failed PR creation leaves a branch that prevents recovery. The “Propose the archived round as a pull request” step pushes its deterministic branch before calling `gh pr create`, then suppresses creation errors. On retry, no open PR is found, so the workflow generates a new commit—including a different `occurred_at` timestamp—and pushes to the existing branch. That push is rejected as non-fast-forward, preventing both PR creation and the subsequent tracking-issue step. Reuse the existing remote branch when retrying PR creation, and surface failures instead of treating an unproposed archive update as successful.
kept_reason: Both findings genuinely fixed in .github/workflows/archive-and-recommend.yml: (1) added a push-to-main reevaluate-on-merge job that re-checks the full merged archive for any topic at/above threshold, closing the multi-pending-PR accumulation gap; (2) the propose-PR step now checks for an existing remote branch before pushing, reusing it on retry instead of attempting a non-fast-forward push, and no longer swallows a genuine gh pr create failure. Both fixes verified against real disposable git-repo scenarios under bash -e, including reproducing the EXACT partial-failure Codex described (pr create fails after the branch is pushed, then a fresh checkout retries) and confirming the retry now succeeds without a non-fast-forward error. CI on PR #2 (commit dabb8c55) confirms the same pattern as every prior round: 12 passed, 1 expected fail-closed, 1 skipped -- nothing existing broke.

findings: **[P2]** **Threshold crossings can be permanently missed.** Each run compares the default-branch archive plus its own round, excluding pending archive PRs. If two rounds together cross the threshold but neither does individually, both runs emit no recommendation. Merging their archive PRs does not trigger this workflow; subsequent reviews see an already-crossed threshold. Reconcile all topics meeting the threshold against existing issues after archive merges, rather than relying exclusively on `newly_crossed`.

**[P2]** **The concurrency configuration drops review rounds.** `cancel-in-progress: false` protects the running workflow, but the default queue allows only one pending run. If A is running and B is pending, arrival of C cancels B, leaving B’s review unarchived. Configure `queue: max` and provide reconciliation for missed runs. See [GitHub’s concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency).

**[P2]** **Archive PR creation cannot reliably recover after a partial failure.** If `git push` succeeds but `gh pr create` fails, the failure is swallowed and the remote branch remains. A rerun finds no open PR, creates a fresh commit on the same branch name, and ordinarily fails with a non-fast-forward push before retrying PR creation. Detect and reuse an existing remote branch, and propagate PR-creation failures so missing archive proposals remain visible and retryable.

findings: **[P2]** `pull-request-analytics-store.ts`: The new query counts matching titles from every session source, although the response describes GitHub-bot reviews. **[P2]** `scripts/analyze-traces.py:114`: Searches cover the entire repository, but `--limit` only restricts hydration. Previously cached traces outside `trace_ids` can contribute matches, so `matching_traces` can exceed `traces_scanned` and results depend on cache history. Restrict matches to the selected trace IDs.

A user or automation session titled `GitHub: Review PR #18` therefore increments the GitHub review metrics without being a bot review. **[P2]** `.github/workflows/analyze-pr-traces.yml` — The notes fetch has no authentication after checkout sets `persist-credentials: false`. On private repositories, it fails even when `refs/notes/traces` exists. The blanket `|| echo` then misreports this as missing notes, allowing analysis to claim there are no linked traces. **[P2]** `scripts/sync-pr-traces.py`, `notes_for_commits()` — The script limits repository-wide notes to 200 **before** filtering for PR commits. **[P2]** `scripts/analyze-traces.py`, `analyze()` — `--limit` controls which traces are listed and hydrated, but topic searches cover the entire directory. Scope searches to the selected trace IDs and handle an empty selection explicitly.

**[P2]** `scripts/analyze-traces.py`, `search_topic()` — Every topic search is capped at 100 results, and `analyze_by_topic()` reports the returned list length as the total. A topic matching more than 100 traces is silently undercounted, including with the default 200-trace scan. Paginate the matches or explicitly report truncated counts.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py:decide` compares current coverage with the parent’s historical coverage on a different archive. Adding unfamiliar findings can therefore trigger a rollback even when the revision still outperforms its parent. For example, adding 20 unclassified findings makes v2 score 26/48, below the recorded 0.6071, while v1 would score only 17/48. Re-measure both policies on the same findings before proposing rollback.

**[P2]** `scripts/improvement_policy.py:append_history` recursively sorts JSON keys, changing topic precedence in stored snapshots. Classification uses the first matching topic, so restoring a snapshot can change existing classifications—for example, alphabetically ordered `auth-lifecycle` takes precedence over `credential-redaction` for “refresh token.” Preserve topic order when serializing snapshots.

**[P2]** `scripts/improvement_policy.py:policy_hash` also sorts topic keys, giving differently ordered classifiers identical hashes. Reordering overlapping topics changes decisions but passes the stale-measurement guard. Hash the ordered topic sequence so the hash captures classification precedence.

**[P2]** `scripts/measure-policy-validity.py:measure_epoch` calculates validity from unweighted recurrence, although the detector uses weighted recurrence and validity repair changes those weights. Consequently, discounting a topic cannot improve measured validity: identical evidence keeps triggering discounts until the minimum weight is reached. Measure the weighted signal used by the detector and evaluate weight revisions against it.

**[P2]** `scripts/measure-policy-validity.py:anchor_counts_at` treats topics missing from an evidence snapshot as having zero matching traces. After a revision adds topics, the workflow reuses the old snapshot, so unsearched topics can be classified as unsupported and have their weights discounted. Bind evidence to the searched taxonomy and treat missing topics as unknown until fresh evidence is collected.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `decide()`: Weight revisions can worsen validity and cannot trigger rollback. For recurrence `[2,1,2,1]`, anchor counts `[1,3,2,0]`, and weights `[0.5,1,1,1]`, restoring the first weight lowers validity from `0.2582` to `0`. The revision is accepted without checking this, and rollback only compares coverage, which weights cannot change. Evaluate candidate validity and include validity regressions in rollback decisions.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `main()`: Measurements are bound to the policy but not the archive. After the archive changes, an old measurement still passes validation. The rollback path then compares stale child coverage against freshly calculated parent coverage, potentially rolling back a child that actually covers more findings. Record and validate an archive digest before making decisions.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `mine_topics()`: Findings matched by companion keywords remain available to support subsequent topics because removal checks only the head token. This already affects the committed policy: the `comment` topic claims two supporting findings, but the finding containing `commit` is classified as `archive-branch`, leaving only one actual match. Remove every finding classified by each newly mined topic before mining the next.

**[P2]** `scripts/measure-policy-validity.py`, `measure()`: Historical replay filters traces by timestamp but includes archive findings solely by round-number prefix. The supplied measurement already includes round 8’s findings in round 9 despite round 8 having a later timestamp. This compares future review evidence against an earlier field snapshot. Apply the epoch timestamp cutoff to archived findings as well.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `decide()`: **Undefined candidate validity passes the acceptance rule.** Reweighting is rejected only when both scores are non-null. For recurrence `[2,1,1,1,1]` and anchor counts `[0,1,2,3,4]`, discounting the first topic changes validity from approximately `-0.7071` to `None`, because weighted recurrence becomes constant. The revision is accepted, subsequent validity triggers stop firing, and the rollback comparison also skips it. Reject candidates that turn a defined validity score into an undefined one.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `decide()`: **The early return prevents corroborated topics from regaining weight.** Restoration runs only when coverage or validity is below its threshold. A topic recurring in four rounds with weight `0.5` can have perfect rank agreement with newly corroborating evidence, yet remain below the mechanism threshold (`2 < 3`) indefinitely. Evaluate supported weight restorations before returning for healthy scores, retaining the non-regression check.

**[P2]** `.github/workflows/revise-improvement-policy.yml`, measurement step: **Configuring the Traces key never enables evidence collection.** Neither measurement command supplies `--repo-dir`; both ignore the installed CLI and key. With the committed empty snapshot, automated validity remains null regardless of new working-session evidence, disabling validity-driven revision and rollback. Add an explicit refresh path using the configured repository scope when a key is available.

**[P2]** `.github/workflows/revise-improvement-policy.yml` commits a stale measurement whenever it revises or rolls back the policy. Measurement runs before the policy changes, and dashboard rendering does not update `measurement.json`. The resulting PR therefore contains a measurement whose hash fails the revision script’s own validation against the accompanying policy. Preserve the original measurement as decision evidence, then regenerate the current measurement after applying the decision.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `decide()`, does not check the complete candidate for validity regression. `weight_repair()` evaluates changes against a baseline that already includes mined topics. If an evidence snapshot contains a topic removed by a rollback, mining that topic again can lower validity and still produce an accepted revision—even with no weight changes. Compare the final candidate’s validity against the original policy before returning `"revise"`; otherwise subsequent runs can repeatedly reintroduce a rejected topic.

**[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `rounds_since()`, measures the rollback waiting period from proposal creation, not adoption. If a policy PR remains open while two archive rounds occur, those rounds satisfy `MIN_ROUNDS_TO_JUDGE` despite running under the previous policy. Once merged, the revision can immediately become eligible for rollback without any rounds under it. Record adoption separately and count subsequent rounds from that point.

**[P2]** `.github/workflows/revise-improvement-policy.yml`: checkout does not pin the default branch. A manual dispatch on a feature branch checks out that branch, so the proposed PR also includes its unrelated, unmerged commits.
